question.text: Meena invested in a mutual fund solely because it was managed by a fund manager who frequently appeared on CNBC-TV18 and had an impressive personality. She assumed a high-profile manager must deliver superior returns. Which behavioral bias is Meena exhibiting?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines Stereo Typing Bias as basing decisions on representative characteristics and gives the example of believing that a high-profile manager implies a better-managed company and a good investment. Meena equates the fund manager's media visibility with expected fund performance — confusing a representative trait with actual investment merit. The Trap: Overconfidence Bias applies when an investor has unwarranted faith in their OWN judgment. Here, Meena is projecting characteristics (media presence, personality) onto an external entity (the fund), which is stereotyping rather than overconfidence. Note: Stereo Typing Bias is one of the behavioural deviations the workbook lists when explaining why investors pick funds for reasons unrelated to fundamentals.
